opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Sloan (employee ID E043) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E043.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Karen Sloan (E043) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin is permitted under policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E043 is a contractor with basic training, contradicting HR's note of full-time. Contractors max out at read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting employment data: HR's note lists E043 as full-time Payroll Specialist, but the Security note (which independently looked up employment type and security training in its own database) states E043 is a contractor with basic training, and explicitly flags the contradiction with HR. Under policy, contractors may have at most read without advanced security training, and admin is never permitted for contractors. Since the request for admin exceeds the maximum of read, I grant the maximum: read.
